t: Addis Ababa began in 1886 as a royal camp beside hot springs, laid out like an army on the march, and became the capital of Menelik II's empire in 1889.

Italian troops entered the city on 5 May 1936 and held it until 1941, when Haile Selassie returned on the fifth anniversary of his departure; later plans by Italian, British and French consultants shaped its growth.
Haile Selassie was deposed in 1974 by the Derg, the EPRDF seized the city in 1991, and the capital became the seat of the Organisation of African Unity and its successor, the African Union.
dyk: The city was first laid out as a katama, a royal camp, with the Imperial Palace in the centre and the lands of the nobles placed on each side as an army is drawn up on the march.
ev: Settlement begins at Finfinne, where Empress Taytu Betul builds a house near the hot springs
Addis Ababa becomes the capital of the Ethiopian Empire
Italian troops enter the city and make it the capital of Italian East Africa
Italian forces kill Ethiopians in Addis Ababa for three days after an attempt on Graziani's life
Haile Selassie returns to Addis Ababa five years to the day after he left
The Organisation of African Unity is formed and keeps its headquarters in the city
Haile Selassie is deposed and the Derg takes power
The Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front seizes the city

f.founded: Settlement began in 1886 at Finfinne, a place of hot springs; the site was chosen by Empress Taytu Betul, and Menelik II, Negus of Shewa, moved his court there. The city became the capital of the empire in 1889.
f.where: In the Ethiopian Highlands at an elevation of 2,355 metres, at the foot of Mount Entoto and on the western edge of the Great Rift Valley, in Ethiopia and surrounded by the Special Zone of Oromia.
f.known: Taytu's house by the hot springs; Menelik II's capital; the Italian occupation of 1936 to 1941; Haile Selassie's return in 1941; the headquarters of the Organisation of African Unity and the African Union; the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa; the Merkato market
f.today: Addis Ababa is the capital and largest city of Ethiopia, a federally chartered city with an estimated 6.3 million inhabitants.
